messages:
maria (infra): Heads-up — we've seen a sustained spike in GPU spend for inference clusters in us-west-2 over the last 10 days. Root cause looks like increase in batch jobs + a handful of untagged spot instances that didn't scale down. Can we sync on approving committed capacity to lock unit price?

nate (ml): :eyes: I noticed some heavy 8k token runs hitting the H100 pool during off hours. Those are killing throughput. Might be some misconfigured eval jobs. I can add caps but we'll still need baseline capacity for production.

maria (infra): Agree. Quick findings from billing-bot: ```
billing-bot: cost_query result: project=redwood-main, period=2026-02-20..2026-03-01, gpu_hours=14,200, est_monthly=$276,000, untagged_gpu_hours=1,900 (~13%).
```

kevin (finance): Thanks for the numbers. Before any commit, need a breakdown: committed vs burstable spend, projected savings for 12m vs 36m, and impact on cashflow. Can you prepare a one-pager?

maria (infra): Will do. Preliminary calc: 36-month reserved H100s would save ~38% per-hour vs on-demand, 12-month save ~22%. For our target baseline of 48 H100s, monthly commit cost approx $115k (12m) vs $90k (36m) vs on-demand ~$185k. Numbers rough — need to validate with cloud pricing API.

zoe (procurement): We also need to decide whether to do a regional commit (us-west-2) or a cross-region contract. Finance typically wants single-region to align with billing. Any risk if we lock only us-west-2?

nate (ml): We have production traffic in eu-central as well but it's <20% of peak. If we reserve in us-west-2 we'll still rely on on-demand in eu for now. That should be okay for Q2 if we keep autoscaling.

kevin (finance): Can we reduce the requested committed quantity? Maybe do a phased commit: start with 32 H100 reserved for 12 months, then reassess. Lower upfront commitment reduces risk.

maria (infra): Phased approach sounds reasonable. Suggest: Phase 1: 32 H100 12m in us-west-2, set up alerts and a cost runway review at 8 weeks. Phase 2: add another 16 or convert to 36m if utilization stays high.

sarah (cto): +1 to phased. Also want to ensure we have fallback plan if jobs shift to eu. Can ops configure automated re-routing to cheaper A100 variants if capacity constrained?

maria (infra): Yes — runtime supports model variant routing. We can fallback to quantized A100 instances for non-latency-critical loads. We'll add routing policy and test in staging before commit.

nate (ml): I'll surface low-priority evals to a scheduler that runs on spot/A100 only. That should drop the off-hour H100 usage by ~25% based on historical job tags.

kevin (finance): For approvals: I'll need an approval memo with (1) final cost table (on-demand vs 12m phased vs 36m), (2) cashflow schedule, (3) list of tag/guardrails we will enforce, (4) who owns revert/scale decisions.

maria (infra): I'll produce the memo. Plan to include: tagging enforcement (deny untagged start), auto-stop for idle GPU > 1h, billing alarms at 60/80/95% of forecasted commit usage, and a runbook for downsizing commit at the renewal point.

zoe (procurement): Also include PO template and timeline. Procurement needs 2 weeks lead time to finalize contract with cloud vendor and legal. Any reason to go multi-cloud for the commit?

kevin (finance): Multi-cloud commits are messy. Prefer single-cloud, single-region commit for now. If we get consistent demand in eu, we'll revisit.

maria (infra): Action items: (a) I'll run precise pricing query and tag audit by EOD tomorrow, (b) Nate will gate non-prod evals to spot/A100, (c) Zoe will start PO checklist, (d) Kevin will draft approval thresholds.

nate (ml): On it — I'll push the scheduler change and ping when done.

billing-bot: scheduled-report uploaded: https://billing.internal/reports/2026-03-gpu-usage — includes tag audit and per-cluster breakdown.

kevin (finance): Great. Once we have the memo, I can route to finance leadership. For the initial ask: approve up to $130k/mo commit (32 H100 equivalent) for 12 months pending the memo. If infra can commit to the tagging/guardrails, I can pre-approve a purchase order hold.

maria (infra): Thanks. I'll aim to have the memo + exact pricing by tomorrow 1700PT. If anything else comes up I'll post here. :thumbsup:

sarah (cto): Thanks team. Keep finance looped. We need to avoid surprises in next ops review.

zoe (procurement): Noted. Starting the vendor checklist now.

maria (infra): Closing note — we should also consider reserved A100s for eu-central if we see sustained growth there. Will monitor and open a separate thread if needed.
